title: PCB trace DC resistance and voltage drop
description: Estimate the DC resistance and voltage-drop magnitude of one uniform rectangular copper trace from its finished geometry.
formula: A = w t; R = rho L / A; V_drop = I R
assumptions: Uniform rectangular finished copper cross-section; resistivity is supplied at the actual conductor temperature.
DC or sufficiently low frequency for nearly uniform current density; no skin/proximity effect, neck-down, contact, via or spreading resistance.
Bulk copper example resistivity 1.7e-8 ohm m is taken from the TI 25-degree-C table; plated copper can differ materially.
One-way conductor resistance, not a complete supply-and-return loop; add the return path separately.

references.title: Texas Instruments, Constructing Your Power Supply - Layout Considerations, Topic 4, section II and Table 1

constraints.message: The finished trace must have a positive copper cross-section.

title: Legacy IPC-2221 trace current screening estimate
description: Compute both legacy external- and internal-layer current estimates for a specified trace cross-section and selected temperature rise; this is not a certified current rating.
formula: A_mil2 = w_mil t_mil; I_external = 0.048 DeltaT^0.44 A_mil2^0.725; I_internal = 0.024 DeltaT^0.44 A_mil2^0.725
assumptions: Legacy empirical IPC-2221 curve-fit as reproduced by TI, not an IPC-2152 implementation or standards-compliance check.
Width and thickness are explicitly in mil, area in mil^2, and temperature rise in degrees C; coefficients cannot be applied directly to SI area.
Screening policy restricts selected temperature rise to 1 through 100 degrees C; this is not a source-certified model validity interval.
Continuous steady current in a uniform trace; no transient/fault-current, via or connector rating is computed.
Board stackup, planes, laminate properties, airflow and local hot spots are absent from the equation; the estimate may be inaccurate and is not guaranteed conservative.
Use finished copper dimensions and verify the actual board thermal environment and voltage-drop requirements separately.

references.title: Texas Instruments TIDA-01232, High-Current Low-Noise Parallel LDO Reference Design, section 3.1.1, Equation 7
IPC-2152 public scope and table of contents: Standard for Determining Current Carrying Capacity in Printed Board Design

constraints.message: Legacy empirical powers require a positive cross-sectional area.

title: Plated via-barrel DC resistance
description: Estimate the axial DC resistance of a cylindrical plated through-hole and an ideal equal-current bank of identical vias.
formula: A = pi p (d + p); R_single = rho L / A; R_bank = R_single / N
assumptions: d is the FINISHED inside hole diameter, p is radial copper plating thickness, and L is the electrically traversed barrel length.
The exact ideal annular copper area is used, not the thin-wall pi d p approximation; no copper-filled via is modeled.
Uniform circular plating, axial current flow, and known plated-copper resistivity at operating temperature; pad spreading, contacts and barrel defects are excluded.
The 6e-8 ohm m plated-copper default is the illustrative value in TI's 2004 table, not a universal modern process property; substitute manufacturer or measured data.
N identical parallel vias share equally only with symmetric low-resistance connections; this calculator provides no via ampacity rating.

references.title: Texas Instruments, Constructing Your Power Supply - Layout Considerations, section II, Table 1 and Figure 3

constraints.message: The parallel via count must be a positive integer.
The plated barrel must have a positive copper cross-section.
